```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
input_file <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
active_file <- if (requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable())
  tryCatch(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path, error = function(e) "") else ""
input_dirs <- c(if (length(input_file) == 1L && !is.na(input_file) && nzchar(input_file)) dirname(input_file),
                if (nzchar(active_file)) dirname(active_file), getwd())
candidates <- unique(unlist(lapply(input_dirs, function(p)
  c(p, file.path(p, ".."), file.path(p, "with_intercept")))))
valid <- vapply(candidates, function(p) file.exists(file.path(p, "R", "gfm_baseline.R")), logical(1))
if (!any(valid)) stop("Cannot locate with_intercept/R/gfm_baseline.R; keep the package directories together.")
project_root <- normalizePath(candidates[which(valid)[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)
baseline_root <- file.path(project_root, "R")
source(file.path(baseline_root, "gfm_baseline.R"), local = knitr::knit_global())
if (!isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress")) || !exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  parsed <- knitr::knit_params(readLines(file.path(project_root, "simulations", "node_inference.Rmd"), warn = FALSE))
  params <- lapply(parsed, function(x) x$value)
}
lambda_values <- if (is.character(params$lambda_values)) {
  as.numeric(trimws(strsplit(params$lambda_values, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]))
} else as.numeric(params$lambda_values)
K <- if (is.null(params$k)) length(lambda_values) else params$k
models <- if (identical(params$model, "all")) c("gaussian", "logit", "poisson", "probit") else params$model
control <- Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
  learning_rate = params$learning_rate, max_iter = params$max_iter,
  tolerance = params$tolerance, M_bound_U = params$M_bound_U,
  M_bound_alpha = params$M_bound_alpha, M_bound_Lambda = params$M_bound_Lambda,
  probability_eps = params$probability_eps,
  max_debias_memory_mb = params$max_debias_memory_mb, backtracking = params$backtracking
))
# NULL selects at most seven workers; 1 selects one.
n_cores <- if (is.null(params$n_cores)) {
  min(7L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) - 1L, na.rm = TRUE))
} else as.integer(params$n_cores)
output_dir <- if (is.null(params$output_dir)) file.path(project_root, "data", "baseline",
  paste0("alpha_", params$alpha_normalization)) else params$output_dir
```

This notebook uses the centered baseline model

\[
\Theta_{ij}^{\star}=\alpha_i^{\star}+\alpha_j^{\star}
  +(u_i^{\star})^\top\Lambda^{\star}u_j^{\star},\qquad
a_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathrm{Uniform}(-2,0),\qquad
\alpha_i^{\star}=a_i/\|a\|_2.
\]

There is one effect per node. The fitted parameter is
$y_i=(u_i^\top,\alpha_i)^\top$, with $K+1$ components.
The uniform support describes the raw draws. Estimation retains the
bounded parameter space and does not constrain the fitted alpha norm.

## Execution controls

The default `run_simulation: false` checks the fixed truth without fitting
networks or writing simulation results. Enable it explicitly for the small
trial configured above. `n_sim` counts networks; `max_iter` limits optimizer
updates for each network. The networks (one per model and replicate) are
fitted in parallel on `n_cores` worker processes; `null` uses at most seven
physical cores and `1` uses one worker. Each network is seeded on its own,
so each task uses its assigned base+r seed independently of scheduling;
floating-point differences can depend on the numerical backend.
YAML controls set to `null` retain the core defaults; non-null values are
passed to `gfb_config()` and recorded with the saved run.

The same $U^\star$, $\alpha^\star$ and $\Lambda^\star$ are held fixed across
all repetitions and observation models. Replicate $r$ uses
`replication_seed_base + r`, seeded separately for each model. The default
three repetitions test execution only; they cannot establish coverage or
asymptotic normality.

Save YAML edits before running setup or Run All. Interactive execution
reloads saved values each time; Knit with Parameters retains supplied overrides.
`worker_backend: "in_process"` and `n_cores: 1` are the portable trial defaults.
For parallel runs explicitly select `worker_backend: "psock"` and a worker count.
This notebook uses the ordinary R implementation for fitting and inference.

The default `alpha_normalization: "l2"` first samples raw
$a_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathrm{Uniform}(-2,0)$, then uses
$\alpha_i^\star=a_i/\sqrt{\sum_j a_j^2}$, so $\|\alpha^\star\|_2=1$.
The transformed components share a random denominator: they are dependent,
are no longer Uniform(-2,0), and their typical scale decreases as $n^{-1/2}$.
This changes the data-generating design, not the estimation constraints,
full-matrix initialization, optimizer controls or BP+BM correction.
Set `alpha_normalization: "none"` to reproduce the original unscaled draws.
Saved truth retains `alpha_raw` and normalization metadata. The default output
and figure paths separate `alpha_l2` from `alpha_none`; an explicitly supplied
`output_dir` or `figure_dir` remains in effect. Do not combine different
generation modes or existing screening results in one evaluation.

## Fixed truth and constraints

```{r truth}
truth <- gfb_generate_truth(
  n = params$n, K = K, lambda_values = lambda_values,
  design_seed = params$design_seed, alpha_seed = params$alpha_seed,
  alpha_min = params$alpha_min, alpha_max = params$alpha_max, alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization
)
truth$diagnostics
data.frame(alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization,
           alpha_raw_l2_norm = sqrt(sum(truth$alpha_raw^2)),
           alpha_model_l2_norm = sqrt(sum(truth$alpha_star^2)))
data.frame(alpha_min_observed = min(truth$alpha_star),
           alpha_max_observed = max(truth$alpha_star),
           max_center_error = max(abs(colSums(truth$U_star))),
           max_orthogonality_error = max(abs(crossprod(truth$U_star) / params$n - diag(K))))
configs <- lapply(models, function(model) {
  gfb_config(n = params$n, K = K, model = model, sigma = params$sigma, control = control)
})
names(configs) <- models
lapply(configs, function(config) config)
```

The design first samples points in the unit ball, centers their columns, then
whitens them so that $\mathbf1^\top U^\star=0$ and
$(U^\star)^\top U^\star=nI_K$. Node effects use their own seed.

## Small experiment

```{r simulate}
simulation <- NULL
if (isTRUE(params$run_simulation)) {
  simulation <- gfb_run_simulation(
    n = params$n, K = K, models = models, n_sim = params$n_sim,
    nodes = params$target_node, lambda_values = lambda_values,
    sigma = params$sigma, design_seed = params$design_seed,
    alpha_seed = params$alpha_seed, replication_seed_base = params$replication_seed_base,
    alpha_min = params$alpha_min, alpha_max = params$alpha_max, alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization,
    control = control, debias = params$debias, debias_method = params$debias_method, output_dir = output_dir,
    run_id = params$run_id, save_fits = params$save_fits,
    n_cores = n_cores,
    worker_backend = params$worker_backend,
    inference_workers = params$inference_workers
  )
  simulation$fit_summary
  cat("Saved run:", simulation$run_dir, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Truth checked. No networks were fitted and no simulation files were written.\n")
}
```

```{r results}
if (!is.null(simulation)) {
  print(table(simulation$fit_summary$model, simulation$fit_summary$status))
  print(simulation$node_summary)
  print(simulation$lambda_summary)
}
```

Failed and unconverged repetitions remain in `fit_summary` and the nested
`records`; inference is skipped when optimization has not converged. The
fit diagnostics also flag binary nodes whose observed edges are all zero or
all one, and Poisson nodes whose edges are all zero, in `one_sided_nodes`.
Such fits are ineligible for inference even when their numerical residual is small.
The node table distinguishes joint standardized coordinates (`z_u1`, ...,
`z_alpha_joint`) from the scalar marginal statistic `alpha_marginal_z`.
Joint whitening generally mixes latent coordinates and the node effect.
The joint quadratic statistic has $K+1$ degrees of freedom.

Each saved run has a fresh directory below `data/baseline/alpha_l2/` by default. Supplying an
already existing `run_id` raises an error, preserving earlier results.
To draw figures from one completed run, pass its `results.rds` path to
`../plots/plot_figures.Rmd`; plotting does not refit networks.

The default `debias_method: "pdf_bp_bm"` retains the baseline
PDF's $B_{P,y_i}=-\frac12\sum_{j\ne i}I_{d,jj}^{-1}(u_i^T,0)^T$
and $DD^T B_P/n^2$ structure, and includes the no-intercept theory's $B_M$
once. Under $\ell=\log p$, code uses $B_1=-\frac12 E[\ell''']$ contractions
and $B_M=E[\ell'\ell'']$ contractions. The additive likelihood correction is
$T(B_1)-T(B_M)$; with the retained negative $B_P$, its additive correction is
$+I_{\Lambda\Lambda}^{-1}I_{\Lambda Y}DD^TB_P/n^2$.
These are explicit sign normalizations of the displayed PDF formulas.

The reviewed finite-sample projector $P=I-D(D^TD)^{-1}D^T$ is retained;
it differs from the literal plug-in $I-DD^T/n$ away from $D^TD=nI$.
Set
`debias_method: "constrained_second_order"` to compare the preserved previous
method; it is not added to the BP/BM correction. Saved results identify the
method and expose `correction_ell3`, `correction_BM` (also named
`correction_score_ell2`), and `correction_constraint` separately.

See `../docs/implementation_notes.md` for the formula mapping and validation scope.
The page-15 argument remains a theoretical question; these implementation
checks do not prove the increasing-dimension limit or normal/chi-square fit.
